questions.question: 'Attolu Eidu' is the cultural festival of which of the following union territories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lakshadweep**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Attolu Eidu'** is a cultural festival celebrated in the **Lakshadweep** Islands, an archipelago of 36 islands located in the **Arabian Sea.**
 
• The festival reflects the **traditional and cultural heritage** of the Lakshadweep community, which is predominantly **Muslim**.
 
• 'Attolu Eidu' is significant as it showcases the **rich traditions, folk music, and dance** unique to this region.
 
• Lakshadweep is known for its **peaceful way of life**, and the festival is an occasion for communal harmony and joy.
 
• The cultural festivities often include performances of **Kolkkali**, a traditional dance form, and other **local art forms**.
 
• The islands are governed as a **Union Territory of India**, and its population has a deep connection to the sea, which influences their festivals and livelihoods.
 
• Lakshadweep's festivals are an important part of its identity, promoting **tourism** and preserving the **islands' unique cultural heritage.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir**__

 __
 
• Jammu and Kashmir is a Union Territory in the northernmost part of India, known for its **Himalayan landscapes and rich cultural heritage.**
 
• It is famous for festivals like **Lohri, Eid-ul-Fitr, and Navroz,** but 'Attolu Eidu' is not celebrated here.
 
 
 
• **Dadra and Nagar Haveli**__
 __
 
• This Union Territory is located in western India and is known for its **tribal culture and festivals** like Tarpa Dance Festival, but it is unrelated to 'Attolu Eidu.'
 
 
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**__
 
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are known for their **Indigenous tribes and natural beauty**, but their cultural festivals are distinct and do not include 'Attolu Eidu.'

questions.question: In which state of India is the Wangala festival celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Meghalaya__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Known as the '100 Drum Festival', the Wangala Festival is a traditional festival in the northeastern Indian state of Meghalaya.
 
• The festival kicked off on November 12th, 2021.
 
• The festival lasts from two days to a week. 
 
• It is one of the most important festivals of the Garo Tribe.
 
• The tribesmen make sacrifices to please their god Saljong. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Wangala festival marks the end of a period of toil, that brings good results to the fields which also signifies the onset of winter.
 
• It is also celebrated in honour of the Sun God that marks the end of the long harvest season.
 
• Wangala is celebrated with different forms of dance.
 
• These dances are performed on the tunes of folk songs that are played on drums and primitive flute.
 
• Additionally, these flutes are made of buffalo horns.
 
• On the first day of the festival, people celebrate it with a ceremony called Ragula.
 
• This ceremony is performed in the house of the village’s chief.
 
• Then on the second day of celebration, which is called Kakkat, people begin the ceremony by dancing to the rhythms of long oval-shaped drums.
 
• In this celebration, young and old join together while men play the drums and women perform traditional dance forms. The dance form is known as Dama Dagota.

questions.question: The religious festival, 'Easter' is celebrated by which community?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Christian community**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Easter** is one of the most significant religious festivals celebrated by the **Christian community worldwide**.
 
• It commemorates the **resurrection of Jesus Christ**, which is believed to have occurred three days after his crucifixion.
 
• **Easter Sunday** marks the end of the Holy Week and the season of Lent, a 40-day period of fasting, prayer, and reflection.
 
• The date of Easter varies each year and is based on the **lunar calendar**, typically falling on the first Sunday after the full moon following the spring equinox.
 
• Easter celebrations often include church services, feasts, and customs like **decorating Easter eggs** and organizing egg hunts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Christianity:**

 
 
• Christianity is a monotheistic religion centered on the life and teachings of Jesus Christ, considered the Son of God.
 
• It is the **world's largest religion**, with over 2.3 billion adherents globally.
 
• Key denominations include Roman Catholicism, Protestantism, and Eastern Orthodoxy.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Easter:**
 
 
• Easter symbolizes hope, renewal, and the victory of life over death.
 
• It is the culmination of the Paschal mystery, which includes Christ's passion, death, and resurrection.
 
 
 
• **Lent:**
 
 
• Lent is a solemn observance lasting 40 days, excluding Sundays, leading up to Easter.
 
• It is characterized by practices such as fasting, prayer, and almsgiving.
 
 
 
• **Easter Traditions:**
 
 
• Common traditions include sunrise services, Easter egg decoration, and festive meals.
 
• The Easter Bunny is a popular secular symbol associated with Easter celebrations.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is associated with the Kamakhya temple of Guwahati?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ambubachi Festival**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Ambubachi Mela **is an **annual Hindu mela**.
 
• It is **held **at **Kamakhya Temple **in **Guwahati, Assam**.
 
• This **yearly Mela **is celebrated **during the monsoon season **that happens to **fall during the Assamese month Ahaar**, around **the middle of June **when the **sun transit to the zodiac of Mithuna**, when the **Brahmaputra river is in spate**.
 
• **Ambubachi **means **spoken with water **and it also **implies that the rains expected during this month **make the **earth fertile and ready for procreation**.
 
• **Daily worship **is **suspended during this period**. All agricultural work like **digging, ploughing, sowing, and transplanting crops is forbidden**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mando **is a **beautiful dance performance**. The theme is usually **one of love **– a **bitter **and **sweet passion **that is slow and **deliberate in movement **and well **expressed through words **and **graceful movements of the dance**.
 
• **Majuli festival **is **celebrated **in the **northeast side of the country**, in the state of **Assam**. The place to **celebrate the festival **is the **bank of River Luit**, which happens to have the **biggest river island in the world**.
 
• **Sunburn **is a commercial **electronic dance music festival **held in **India**. From **2007 to 2015**, it took **place in Vagator**, **Goa**, India every year, but in **2016 it was shifted to Pune**, **Maharashtra**.

questions.question: With which of the following states is the 'Banganga' Festival associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Banganga** festival is celebrated at **Malabar Hills, Mumbai**.
 
• It is an **annual music festival celebrated for 2 days **particularly at **Malabar Hills, in Mumbai Maharashtra**.
 
• It is celebrated every year in the **month of January **jointly by **Maharashtra Tourism Development Corporation and Indian Heritage society Mumbai**.
 
• Its name is based on a holy water tank named **Banganga Tank in the Walkeshwar Temple complex at Malabar Hills**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The festival was first celebrated in **1992**.
 
• Classical music performances are given by **classical musicians from all over the country to promote and conserve our cultural heritage**.
 
• The ** Walkeshwar Temple was constructed between the 9th and 13th** centuries by the Sahara dynasty.
 
• **The Banganga tank** is constructed along with the temple for** water conservation**.
 
• It was destroyed by the** Portuguese later it was renovated in 1715**.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Alpasi Festival celebrated annually, where a holy bath of the deities in the sea is the primary attraction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Alpasi Festival** is an annual religious festival celebrated in **Kerala**.
 
• It is one of the major festivals at the **Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple** in Thiruvananthapuram.
 
• The festival features a significant event where the **deities are given a holy bath** in the sea, which is the primary attraction.
 
• This ritual is known as the **Arattu** and involves a procession from the temple to the beach.
 
• The festival showcases the rich **cultural and religious heritage** of Kerala.
 
• It typically occurs during the **Malayalam month of Thulam** (October-November).
 
• The Alpasi Festival is marked by elaborate **ceremonies, rituals, and traditional art forms**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Andhra Pradesh**__

 __
 
• Andhra Pradesh is known for its **rich cultural heritage** and festivals such as **Ugadi, Sankranti, and Dussehra**.
 
• It is famous for the **Tirupati Balaji Temple**, a significant pilgrimage site.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka**__
 __
 
• Karnataka is known for festivals like **Dasara** in Mysore, which is celebrated with grandeur.
 
• It is famous for its historical sites like **Hampi** and **Mysore Palace**.
 
 
 
• **Telangana**__
 
 
• Telangana celebrates festivals like **Bathukamma** and **Bonalu**, which are unique to the region.
 
• It is known for the **Charminar** and **Golconda Fort** in Hyderabad.

questions.question: Tusu is a harvest festival celebrated in Jharkhand during the winter in the last day of _______ month.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Poush.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tusu** is a **harvest festival **celebrated in **Jharkhand **during the** winter season.**
 
• It is celebrated on the **last day** of the **Poush month**, which usually falls in **January.**
 
• The festival is primarily celebrated by the **tribal communities **in Jharkhand.
 
• Tusu is a** symbol of gratitude** towards nature and its **bountiful resources.**
 
• During the festival, people dress up in** traditional attire**, perform **cultural dances** and **sing songs** in praise of nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phalguna **is the **twelfth month** of the Hindu calendar and falls between **February and March**. 

 
 
• It is the month of** Holi,** the festival of colors.
 
 
 
• **Chaitra** is the first month of the Hindu calendar and falls between **March and April.**
 
 
• It marks the** beginning of the new year** in many parts of India.
 
 
 
• **Magha** is the** eleventh month** of the Hindu calendar and falls between **January and February.**
 
 
• It is considered an auspicious month for performing **religious rituals.**
 
 
 
• **Poush** is the** tenth month **of the Hindu calendar and falls between **December and January**. 
 
 
• It is a month of **harvest festivals** celebrated in many parts of India.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 4, Poush.**

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated when the annual harvest takes place in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magh Bihu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** Magh Bihu:

__
 
• Bihu is a traditional festival of the state of Assam.
 
• Magh Bihu is celebrated on the 14 and 15 of January (1st and 2nd Magh, the tenth month of the Assamese calendar).
 
• The first day is called Uruka.
 
• That day people build a temporary shed called Bhela Ghar and have a community feast.
 
• Bora is a common variety of rice used in Assam.
 
• These are* ‘sticky’ *rice. 
 
• People also eat cheva rice and pitha with tea.
 
• People also roast sweet potatoes.
 
• To prepare Cheva rice, fire is lit and water is kept to boil in a big tao (a big vessel).
 
• On this vessel, the Kadhahi containing the soaked rice is kept and covered with banana leaves.
 
• After some time, the cheva rice is cooked and ready to eat.
 
• People eat and dance together and enjoy the festivities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
